# BAA-Equivalent Confidentiality Addendum (Template)

> Confidentiality and privileged-information addendum scoped to law firms and other professional-services customers. Internal drafting template; not a final form.

---

## When to use this template

This addendum is required when Customer is a law firm. For other professional-services customers (healthcare practices, accounting firms, advisory firms), equivalent confidentiality terms apply on a case-by-case basis as determined by Captain in consultation with external counsel. Where Customer is a HIPAA-covered entity or business associate, a separate HIPAA Business Associate Agreement may be required in addition to or in place of this addendum, depending on the scope of protected health information involved.

The name "BAA-equivalent" reflects that this addendum performs the equivalent function for attorney-client privileged and work-product material that a Business Associate Agreement performs for protected health information: it documents the confidentiality regime, the permitted uses, the handling of compelled disclosure, and the lifecycle of the protected category at the end of the engagement.

# BAA-Equivalent Confidentiality Addendum

**This BAA-Equivalent Confidentiality Addendum (this "Addendum") is entered into as of [EFFECTIVE DATE] (the "Effective Date") between SMDurgan, LLC (d/b/a SMD Services) ("SMD") and [CUSTOMER LEGAL NAME] ("Customer"). This Addendum forms part of and is incorporated by reference into the AI Employee Service Agreement between the Parties dated [EFFECTIVE DATE] (the "Service Agreement") and the Data Processing Addendum executed concurrently with the Service Agreement (the "DPA"). Capitalized terms not defined in this Addendum have the meanings given in the Service Agreement and the DPA.**

## 1. Purpose and Acknowledgements

1.1 Customer is a professional-services firm that handles information subject to industry-specific confidentiality obligations, including (as applicable) attorney-client privileged communications, attorney work product, fiduciary obligations, and other categories of legally protected information.

1.2 The Parties acknowledge that the AI Employee Service, in the ordinary course of producing drafts and surfacing them to Reviewers, will read substantive content that includes or relates to Protected Information (as defined in Section 2).

1.3 This Addendum supplements and does not limit the confidentiality, security, and data-handling commitments in the Service Agreement and the DPA. To the extent of any conflict between this Addendum and the Service Agreement or DPA with respect to Protected Information, this Addendum controls.

1.4 Nothing in this Addendum is intended to create a fiduciary, attorney-client, or other professional relationship between SMD and any third party (including Customer's clients). SMD is a vendor providing software services to Customer.

## 2. Definitions

2.1 **"Protected Information"** means information accessed, observed, processed, or generated by the AI Employee in the course of providing the Service to Customer that falls within any of the following categories:

(a) **Privileged communications**: communications subject to the attorney-client privilege or any analogous evidentiary privilege recognized in the governing jurisdiction.

(b) **Work product**: materials prepared by Customer or Customer's personnel in anticipation of litigation or for trial, including mental impressions, conclusions, opinions, legal theories, and litigation strategy.

(c) **Client confidences**: information of any of Customer's clients held by Customer in a fiduciary or professional capacity, including information that would be protected by professional rules of confidentiality applicable to Customer's profession (for example, ABA Model Rule 1.6 for U.S. lawyers and analogous rules in other professions and jurisdictions).

(d) **Sensitive personal data**: data of any client or counterparty that constitutes a special category of personal data under applicable privacy law, where the AI Employee accesses such data in the course of producing a draft.

2.2 **"Matter"** means any client engagement, file, case, or other discrete unit of work in Customer's practice for which the AI Employee accesses or produces Protected Information.

## 3. Permitted Uses

3.1 SMD will access and process Protected Information solely for the purposes set forth in Section 3 of the DPA. SMD will not use Protected Information for any other purpose, including SMD's own product development, marketing, training of any machine-learning model (consistent with DPA Section 4.1), or for the benefit of any other SMD customer (consistent with DPA Section 4.6).

3.2 SMD will not disclose Protected Information to any third party, including any Sub-processor, except as necessary to provide the Service and subject to the Sub-processor restrictions in DPA Section 5. Sub-processors that receive Protected Information through the Service are bound by written terms imposing protection no less stringent than this Addendum.

3.3 SMD will not segregate, aggregate, analyze, or otherwise use Protected Information for the purpose of developing insights about Customer's clients, Customer's matters, or Customer's adversaries.

## 4. Closed-Loop Reinforcement for Protected Information

4.1 The closed-loop architecture commitments in DPA Section 4 apply with full force to Protected Information. In particular:

(a) Substantive Matter content (privileged communications, work product, client documents) is read at active draft time only and is not persisted into the Memory Artifact or any Sub-processor's storage, consistent with DPA Section 4.3.

(b) The Memory Artifact retains only Customer-curated and structural-diff content per DPA Section 4.2. The Memory Artifact does not contain the substantive text of privileged communications or work product.

(c) Every customer-bound external message related to a Matter is sent under a Reviewer's identity per [ADR 0005](../../adr/0005-reviewer-as-sender.md). The AI Employee does not send communications to clients, opposing counsel, courts, or other third parties under its own identity.

(d) Customer's Machine is exclusive to Customer per [ADR 0007](../../adr/0007-per-customer-machine-isolation.md). No other SMD customer's Machine has any path to read, infer from, or learn from Customer's Protected Information per [ADR 0009](../../adr/0009-cross-machine-query-prohibition.md).

4.2 SMD acknowledges the importance of the closed-loop posture for the preservation of attorney-client privilege and work product. The Parties' shared understanding is that the architectural commitments in this Section 4 are intended to support, and not to weaken, Customer's privilege and work-product positions vis-a-vis third parties. The Parties acknowledge that whether privilege is preserved in any specific situation is ultimately a determination for Customer's licensed counsel and for the relevant tribunal, and is not warranted by SMD.

## 5. Vendor-Hostile-Content Sources

5.1 Some third-party content vendors that Customer's profession relies upon (for example, legal research databases) prohibit ingestion of their content into third-party AI. The platform enforces these prohibitions at the connector layer per DPA Section 5.5 and Platform PRD §13.4.

5.2 Where Customer connects such a source, the platform's "do-not-ingest" connector flag is enabled by default. Content from such sources is read by Customer's human users only and is not provided to the AI Employee for context, drafting, or memory.

## 6. Conflicts of Interest

6.1 SMD is a service vendor and does not, in its own right, owe Customer's clients duties of loyalty, confidentiality, or care. SMD will, however, take the following operational steps to avoid creating circumstances that complicate Customer's conflict checks:

(a) **Cross-customer prohibition.** SMD's architecture prevents one customer's data from informing another customer's runtime per DPA Section 4.6 and [ADR 0009](../../adr/0009-cross-machine-query-prohibition.md). This control eliminates the most direct technical pathway for cross-customer informational flow.

(b) **Operational conflict notification.** If SMD becomes aware that it provides services to multiple firms that may have adverse interests in a known Matter, SMD will notify Customer within [CONFLICT NOTIFICATION DAYS] days of becoming aware, to the extent that providing notice does not itself constitute a breach of another customer's confidentiality. The notification will identify the existence of the potential adversity at a level of generality consistent with SMD's confidentiality obligations to other customers and will not disclose the other customer's matters, clients, or substantive content.

(c) **No representations about conflict status.** SMD does not represent or warrant that its customer base is conflict-free with respect to any specific Matter. Customer remains solely responsible for performing conflict checks under the rules applicable to Customer's profession.

## 7. Compelled Disclosure and Legal Process

7.1 **Notification.** If SMD receives a subpoena, court order, search warrant, civil investigative demand, or other compulsory legal process seeking Protected Information, SMD will, except to the extent prohibited by law:

(a) notify Customer in writing within [SUBPOENA NOTIFICATION HOURS] hours of receipt;

(b) provide Customer with a copy of the process and the identity of the issuing authority;

(c) not produce Protected Information until Customer has had a reasonable opportunity to object, move to quash, seek a protective order, or otherwise respond; and

(d) reasonably cooperate (at Customer's expense) with Customer's efforts to challenge or limit the scope of the process.

7.2 **Scope of production.** If, after Customer has had a reasonable opportunity to respond and any challenge has been resolved, SMD is required to produce Protected Information, SMD will produce only the minimum information legally required and will request confidential treatment (including filing under seal where applicable).

7.3 **Audit log distinction.** SMD's audit log contains metadata (timestamps, actor identifiers, action types, content digests) but does not contain the substantive text of privileged communications. Production of audit log content does not, by itself, disclose the substantive content of any privileged communication.

7.4 **No voluntary disclosure.** SMD will not voluntarily disclose Protected Information to any third party, including law enforcement, in the absence of compulsory process, except with Customer's prior written consent or as expressly required by law.

## 8. Retention of Protected Information

8.1 Retention of Protected Information follows the retention regime in DPA Section 10, with the following clarifications specific to Protected Information:

(a) **No retention of substantive Matter content.** Because substantive Matter content is read at draft time only and is not persisted into the Memory Artifact per Section 4.1, there is no SMD-side retention period for the substantive text of privileged communications or work product. The substantive content remains where it lives in Customer's connected systems.

(b) **Structural-diff retention.** Structural-diff records that record formatting patterns from Customer's edits are retained per Customer's configured retention window per Platform PRD §10.4. These records do not contain substantive Matter content.

(c) **Audit log retention.** Audit log entries that reference Matter activity (timestamps, actor identifiers, action types, content digests, Matter reference identifiers) are retained per DPA Section 10.4. Audit log entries contain content digests, not substantive content.

8.2 On termination of the Service Agreement, the destruction of Protected Information remaining in SMD-controlled storage occurs as part of the decommissioning procedure documented in the [decommission spec](../../specs/ai-employee/decommission-customer.md) and DPA Section 10.3. SMD will provide written confirmation of decommissioning to Customer within [OFFBOARDING WINDOW DAYS] days of the Effective Termination Date.

8.3 If Customer's professional rules require return rather than destruction of Protected Information at engagement end, the memory export per DPA Section 11 satisfies the return obligation for the portion of Protected Information SMD held.

## 9. Disclosure Posture

9.1 The AI Employee's role in Customer's practice is an internal operational matter. Whether and how Customer discloses the AI Employee's involvement to Customer's clients, courts, regulators, or other third parties is governed by the professional and ethical rules applicable to Customer.

9.2 SMD will support Customer's disclosure choices through the platform's configurable disclosure mechanisms per Platform PRD §13.2, including (for law firms) per-jurisdiction engagement-letter clause libraries and signature-footer disclosure clauses.

9.3 The platform's compliance evidence packet per Platform PRD §13.6 is designed to allow Customer's ethics counsel or outside counsel to verify the closed-loop posture without requiring access to substantive Matter content.

## 10. Personnel and Access

10.1 SMD personnel with access to Customer's Machine, namespaces, or operational infrastructure are subject to confidentiality obligations no less protective than this Addendum. SMD will train such personnel on the importance of the confidentiality regime for professional-services customers.

10.2 SMD's operational access to Customer's Machine and namespaces is logged in the SMD operational audit trail per DPA Section 7.1(d). Customer may request a summary of access events affecting Customer in any twelve-month period.

## 11. Breach Notification

11.1 In addition to the Security Incident notification obligations in DPA Section 8, SMD will, in the case of a Security Incident affecting Protected Information, expressly identify the Protected Information categories affected and provide Customer with reasonable cooperation in fulfilling any notification obligations Customer owes to clients, bar associations, regulators, or other authorities under the professional rules applicable to Customer.

## 12. Remedies

12.1 Customer's remedies for breach of this Addendum are cumulative with the remedies available under the Service Agreement and DPA. The Parties acknowledge that monetary damages may not be an adequate remedy for breaches affecting Protected Information and that Customer may seek injunctive or other equitable relief.

12.2 The liability cap in Service Agreement Section 11.1 does not apply to breaches of this Addendum or DPA Section 4 to the extent that the breach constitutes gross negligence or willful misconduct, consistent with Service Agreement Section 11.3.

## 13. Governing Law and Survival

13.1 This Addendum is governed by the law of [GOVERNING LAW STATE] consistent with Service Agreement Section 13.4.

13.2 Sections 7 (with respect to compelled disclosure events occurring during the Term), 8.2, 11, and 12 survive termination of this Addendum for the periods stated or as required by applicable law and applicable professional rules.
